feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-driven achievements, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page site migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and broad platform ownership.  
- Professional, readable tone with relevant expertise spanning strategy, CMS, analytics, governance, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign results. This will sharpen impact.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—consider “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven communications leadership.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter phrase like “multi-channel digital programs.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, web and CMS modernization, editorial workflows, and cross-functional coordination. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content that supports advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and organizational goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel/multi-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” and “advocacy messaging” also recur elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform management & CMS modernization.”
- Reduce repetition around workflows by combining “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one clearer competency.
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles: digital transformation, Drupal/web modernization, analytics infrastructure, governance, and advocacy communications.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform management & CMS modernization • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Public-sector policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially analytics, multimedia, and editorial systems.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise web modernization, campaign infrastructure, and content operations for member-facing digital communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes: “Designed/implemented Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsite architecture, and downloadable toolkits to improve reuse, publishing speed, or engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points: digital strategy/governance; Drupal/CMS delivery; analytics/workflows; AI-enabled search initiative.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing teams enabled, reduction in manual steps, faster launch timelines, search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and organization-wide communications” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this item focused on consulting impact since Oct. 2024.
- Specific projects like the microsite and AI search already appear in Recent Projects; mention them briefly here without repeating feature-level detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel ownership more specific or measurable: add email open/click gains, audience growth, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets; emphasize scale/capability expansion here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows clear growth into the Director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” and “Produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” / “strengthened” with direct ownership: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes” or “Standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director role; keep this item focused on hands-on operations rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing strategic leadership rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with the operational leadership shown in recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section more directly to scale/complexity rather than outcomes here, since metrics belong better in Work Experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” already echo the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than tool inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or older items unless job-relevant: consider dropping “jQuery” and possibly “WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages” from this topline section if they are already listed in Technical + IT.
- Use more strategic phrasing aligned to recent work: “Enterprise web platforms” or “CMS modernization and technical delivery” is stronger than naming multiple platforms upfront.
- If space allows, prioritize what is most evidenced in recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow integration, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as concise capability phrases, not just platforms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity”
- Add business value: “analytics infrastructure, KPI framework design, executive reporting, and performance optimization”
- Tighten the last item: replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX, and content performance analysis”
- Possible rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • SEO, UX, and content performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Leadership reporting” may be clearer as “executive reporting,” which aligns better with senior-level positioning.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and recent studio/event capability rather than basic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “End-to-end video production” or “Broadcast-quality multimedia production”
- Consider adding scale/outcome if space allows: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy programming and recurring organizational events”
- Keep to 3–4 bullets max; remove lower-value wording like “virtual event production” if “hybrid event delivery” already covers it

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use more specific phrasing here to avoid repetition
- “Studio operations” is supported by the Director of Digital Media entry, so align wording with that recent achievement rather than older production tasks

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine only if Drupal remains clearly first; consider dropping GitHub Pages if space is tight.
- Add light qualifiers to show level/value, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content systems) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- If formatting allows, split by strength: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Working knowledge: Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or differentiating this one with proficiency labels.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding labels.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at this level.
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management (Google Tag Manager)” to show applied use, not just tool familiarity.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating GitHub Actions unless this section is the primary technical tools list.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as an undifferentiated software list. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should emphasize systems you actually used to build/coordinate workflows, not generic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Project Systems**
- Tighten to higher-signal tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g.: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project and editorial coordination)**
- Move **Slack • Teams • Basecamp • Trello** to a broader “Collaboration Tools” line only if space allows; otherwise cut them as lower-value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same idea without adding specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four can look padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize leading email/newsletter operations, this item should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, not just names.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaign operations, newsletter distribution, audience engagement workflows)**
- If accurate, add scope to make it stronger: **…supporting newsletters to tens of thousands of stakeholders** or **enterprise/member communications**
- Put the most relevant/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 was only light exposure, lead with **Higher Logic** instead
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening to **Dynamics 365 CI/Journeys** if space is tight

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email/newsletter channels; avoid repeating audience size here unless the experience bullets stay less specific
- “Engagement” is already implied elsewhere in multi-channel communications, so focus this line on platforms + email operations context

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh support, and multimedia delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/traffic, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly video updates, or channels supported.
- Tighten phrasing and foreground impact: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” only if that reflects actual responsibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this entry, frame it as launching or early production rather than expansion.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is echoed in later roles; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize initiative, scope, and any concrete outputs to make it worth keeping.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to highlight ownership and first-of-its-kind impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; expanded communications support through digital and multimedia content production.”
- Tighten the podcast line: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add measurable detail: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a sharper two-line version: “Coordinated innovation and research projects for county-focused policy and program initiatives. Helped produce digital and multimedia content and launched NACo’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this item focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad digital operations language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
